questions.stem: Duncan bought a generator from Quality Company Ltd and informed the seller that he was buying it for his sister Stella. After one month, the generator exploded and Stella sued Quality Company Ltd for damages. Examine all the issues, and explain whether her action, would succeed. Support your answer with authorities. In another case, Duncan contracted to use Metropolitan event hall for his event on the 31st of May 2026 but on the 10th of May, the proprietors of the event hall informed him in writing that the hall will not be available 31st due to certain problems. He approached a Barrister Kanu who advised him to sue immediately but since that didn't sound reasonable, he approached another Barrister called Eyo who told him to wait and sue on the 3rd of May if they still fail to release the hall to him. Should Duncan sue? Whose advice should he rely on? Support your answer with authority.

Briefly state the facts and principles established by the following cases: Attorney General of Adamawa State & Ors v Attorney General of the Federation (2014) 1 LPELR-2321(SC); Arowolo v Fabiyi (1995) 8 NWLR (Pt.414) 496; and British Airways v Atoyebi (2014) 13 NWLR (PT. 1424) 253

(a) Mrs Adebayo, a registered nurse, entered into a contract with Mr Musa to import drugs into Nigeria for distribution. Mr Adebayo paid 25 million naira to Mr Musa to facilitate the importation. It is legally required that only a licensed pharmacist can import such drugs, stating its composition on the invoice. Mrs Adebayo paid an additional 5 million naira for delivery to her. The goods were seized by government officials, and she seeks to recover the monies paid to Mr Musa. Advise Mrs Adebayo as regards the transaction. Would your answer be different if the additional 5 million was an inducement?

(b) Mr. James, a 75-year-old widower, owned several valuable properties and operated a successful business. Due to ill health, he relied heavily on his nephew, Peter, who managed his financial affairs and accompanied him to all business meetings. One day, Peter insisted that Mr James transfer ownership of one of his commercial buildings to him. Peter threatened to stop paying for Mr. James's medical treatment and to abandon him if he refused. Feeling vulnerable and fearing for his well-being, Mr. James introduced Mr. James to a businessman, Mr. Bello, who offered to purchase another of Peter introduced Mr. James to a businessman, Mr. Bello, who offered to purchase another of Mr. James's properties at a price significantly below its market value. During the negotiations, Peter repeatedly assured Mr. James that the transaction was in his best interest and discouraged him from seeking independent legal advice. Mr. James eventually signed the agreement. After recovering from his illness, Mr. James now wishes to challenge both transactions. (a) Examine the legal concepts of duress and undue influence, distinguishing between the two doctrines. (b) Discuss whether Peter's conduct in relation to the transfer of the commercial building amounts to duress. In your answer, distinguish between actual undue influence and presumed undue influence.

(a) In January 2026, Mr Bassey a businessman decided to venture into petroleum business. In furtherance to this, Bassey saw, negotiated and paid for a land along Calabar Road for his fueling station. Bassey was lucky to pay just 20million for such a strategic land. David who sold the land to Bassey later sold the same land to Ndiok for 40million. Ndiok immediately and hastily started building a hotel on the land. Bassey confronted David and the latter presented that he Bassey a cheque of 20million as refund. Frustrated, Bassey rejected the refund insisting that he must build on the land. With the aid of legal principles and case law, advise Bassey on the immediate, short-term and permanent legal solution available.

(b) The University of Calabar entered into a contract with Ubong for the supply of hundred units of tenth generation laptops at 987 thousand Naira each. Ubong is required to supply and install all the gadgets at the University computer centre before payment. Ubong contacted his suppliers in Lagos for the laptops and paid for the hundred units at 687 thousand Naira per unit. In fact, Ubong used his entire life savings and even got a loan to pay for the laptops. Suddenly, the University revoked the contract and award same to another person. As a result, Ubong became ill and developed high blood pressure. He has so far spent 40 million on his health. The interest on the loan he collected for the contract is increasing monthly. All Ubong's children at now out of school due to the revocation of the contract. To make matters worse, Ubong just got a quit notice from his landlord because of unpaid rent. With the aid of case law, mention the processes and the exact amount the court would likely award if Ubong succeeds.

(c) Chief Gregory agreed to buy a house from Nelson, unknown to both of them that the land had be destroyed by fire two days before they signed the contract, and now. Mr Nelson sues Gregory for the price. In another case, Nelson offers to sell a plot of land to Chief Gregory for 3 million, who knowing that Nelson meant 30 million, accepts the offer and tenders 3 million. Which Nelson refuses to collect but rather sues him to pay 30 million. Chief Gregory in his response, is asking the court to grant an order of specific performance. In yet another case, Nelson told Chief Gregory: "this car has never had any accident". Relying on this, Chief Gregory bought the car. Gregory discovered a few weeks after buying that the car was badly smashed and is considering suing Mr Nelson. What remedies does he have, if any?
